contents.text: Aircraft Wing
A primary aerodynamic component that generates lift and supports stable flight.
Jet Engine
A propulsion system that generates thrust to power the aircraft during flight.
ECAM Display
The display shows information on the engine and key systems, assisting the pilot in monitoring status and alerts during flight.
Thrust Levers
Cockpit controls used by the pilot to adjust engine thrust and manage aircraft power.
Rudder Pedals
Foot-operated controls used by the pilot to control the aircraft’s rudder and yaw.
Steering Tiller
A cockpit control used to steer the aircraft’s nose wheel during ground operations.
Aircraft passenger cabin
The enclosed section of an aircraft designed to accommodate passengers during flight.
Drag Brace
A structural support component that helps secure and stabilize the aircraft landing gear during operation.
Torque Link
A landing gear component that prevents unwanted rotation and keeps the strut properly aligned.
Oleo Strut
A shock-absorbing landing gear component that uses hydraulic fluid and compressed gas to absorb landing loads.
Nose Landing Gear Wheel
A wheel assembly that supports the aircraft’s nose and enables smooth ground movement during taxiing, takeoff, and landing.
Fan Blades
Generates thrust by accelerating a large volume of incoming air.
Fan Spinner
Streamlines airflow into the fan and reduces aerodynamic drag.
Fan Case
Houses and supports the fan assembly while guiding incoming airflow.
Piping & Harness
Routes fluids, electrical power, and sensor signals throughout the engine.
Structural Support Frame
Supports major engine components and maintains structural alignment.
Bleed Air System
Extracts compressed air from the engine for cooling, pressurization, and other aircraft systems.
Exhaust Nozzle
Directs and accelerates exhaust gases as they leave the engine.
Tail Cone
Shapes the exhaust flow around the engine centerline and helps reduce turbulence.
Low Pressure Turbine
Extracts energy from exhaust gases to drive the low-pressure spool.
